name: Guernsey
summary: Crown Dependency outside the UK and EU. No capital gains tax, no inheritance or gift tax, no wealth tax. Income including dividends is taxed at a flat 20%, with optional caps of £160,000 (foreign income) or £320,000 (worldwide), and a £60,000 cap for four years for newcomers buying Open Market property. A GST was approved in October 2026 (from about 2028).

regimes.name: Ordinary Guernsey residence
regimes.description: Residents pay a flat 20% income tax on worldwide income. No capital gains, inheritance, gift or wealth tax; probate fee about 0.5% of personal estate, capped at £250,000.
regimes.eligibility: Tax residence in Guernsey. Newcomers without local housing status can generally only live in Open Market (Part A) housing.

capital_gains.summary: Guernsey has no capital gains tax. Gains by a resident private investor on securities, a private business or real estate are not taxed unless the activity is a trade (taxed as income at 20%).

capital_gains.rate_basis: No capital gains tax (Carey Olsen: 'no ... capital gains taxes'); income tax at 20% applies to income only.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Dealing in shares or land as a trade is taxed as income at 20%; Guernsey property development profits are taxed at 20%.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: From 2026, repayments of non-commercial shareholder loans from personal investment companies are treated as dividends (anti-avoidance).

dividends.summary: Dividends are taxed as income at a flat 20%. Guernsey companies paying dividends to resident individuals deduct tax at source up to 20% (20% if the company paid 0%). Residents can elect tax caps (see special regimes).

Guernsey Income Tax (Revenue Service guide, section C: relief for tax paid in other countries)

dividends.rate_basis: Flat 20% income tax rate on net income after allowances (PwC). Personal allowance £15,200 for 2026, withdrawn above £85,000 of income. Foreign tax relief where there is no treaty (unilateral relief) is the lower of the foreign tax and three-quarters of the effective Guernsey rate of tax on the income (Revenue Service guide): at the 20% top rate that is 15% of the gross dividend, so a 15% withholding is credited in full.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Personal allowance £15,200 (2026), withdrawn from £85,000 of income.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 0% withholding on dividends to non-residents under domestic law; dividends to Guernsey-resident individuals carry a deduction making up tax to 20%.
dividends.treaty_network: 14 comprehensive double tax agreements (incl. UK, Jersey, Isle of Man, Luxembourg, Malta, Cyprus, Singapore, Hong Kong); no US income tax treaty, so US dividends suffer 30% US withholding. Foreign tax relieved by credit.
open_questions: Credit relief mechanics for non-treaty source countries not verified from Revenue Service guidance.
The Revenue Service guide read for unilateral relief is a 2017 document; the related Statement of Practice M8 was withdrawn on 19 August 2024 and its replacement was not found.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Modelled as the 'holding_company' structure regime: a Guernsey company pays 0% on investment income and gains; a distribution to a Guernsey-resident member bears a 20% charge deducted by the company when its income was taxed at less than 20% (Revenue Service).

wealth_tax.summary: No wealth tax or net worth tax.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Tax on Real Property (TRP) is an annual property tax based on property size and use (not a wealth tax). Document duty applies to property purchases; the extra 2% on second/buy-to-let properties was removed in the 2026 Budget.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax. A probate registry fee applies to personal (movable) estate: £225 up to £80,000 plus £50 per further £10,000 (0.5%), capped at £250,000 for estates above about £50m. Worldwide personal estate counts if no grant has been taken elsewhere.

sources.title: Probate and estate administration for Guernsey domiciliaries

inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Probate Registry fee on the gross value of the personal estate (no deduction for debts): GBP 225 plus GBP 50 for each additional GBP 10,000 above GBP 80,000, plus small amounts for extra documents; capped at GBP 250,000 above GBP 50,030,000 (Mourant guide of 27 February 2026). Guernsey real property is outside the grant. Older guides (Carey Olsen 2020) show GBP 35 per GBP 10,000 (0.35%), so the scale has risen. Not indexed. The official fee order was not found.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Lifetime gifts attract no fee, and assets already covered by a foreign grant are valued on the Guernsey estate only.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Worldwide movable estate counts for the probate fee unless probate has been obtained in another jurisdiction.
inheritance.domicile_rules: No tax, so no domicile test for tax. Families arriving from the UK remain within UK IHT under the residence-based test from 6 April 2025 for up to 10 years after leaving, depending on years of UK residence.
open_questions: Official Probate Registry fee schedule not located; figures from Mourant guide dated 27 Feb 2026.

regimes.name: Income tax cap
regimes.description: A Guernsey resident can elect to cap income tax on non-Guernsey-source income (including Guernsey bank interest) at £160,000 a year, or on worldwide income at £320,000 a year (2026, unchanged since 2024). Guernsey property income is taxed at 20% on top. Since 2023 each spouse elects individually.
regimes.eligibility: Any Guernsey-resident individual, by annual election. Worthwhile when 20% of foreign income exceeds £160,000 (about £800,000 of income).

lump_sum.notes: £160,000 is a maximum, not a fixed charge: tax is the lower of 20% of non-Guernsey income and the cap. The £320,000 cap covers worldwide income. Per individual since independent taxation in 2023 (couple: up to £320,000 on foreign income). Modelled as a maximum (is_cap): the family pays the lower of the cap and the ordinary tax on the income it covers; per individual since 2023 (Revenue Service, tax caps).

dividends.summary: Once the £160,000 cap binds, further foreign dividends carry no Guernsey tax. Guernsey-source dividends stay at 20% unless the £320,000 worldwide cap is chosen.

regimes.duration_note: No time limit: any Guernsey resident can claim the cap each year under sections 39B-39E and the Sixth Schedule of the Income Tax (Guernsey) Law, 1975 (gov.gg tax cap page). The cap amounts are set in each annual Budget; it is apportioned in the year of arrival or departure.

regimes.name: Open Market new-resident tax cap
regimes.description: A newcomer who buys an Open Market (Part A) property with at least £50,000 of document duty can cap income tax on worldwide income (except Guernsey property income) at £60,000 a year for the arrival year and the following three years. After that the ordinary caps apply.
regimes.eligibility: Not Guernsey resident in the previous three years; purchase of a Part A Open Market property within 12 months of becoming resident, paying at least £50,000 document duty (roughly a £1.3m+ property).

lump_sum.notes: Maximum, not a fixed charge. Guernsey land and property income excluded (taxed at 20%). Amount £60,000 since 2024, unchanged for 2026. A June 2026 proposal by Innovate Guernsey to raise it has not been adopted as far as found. Modelled as a maximum (is_cap): the family pays the lower of the cap and the ordinary tax on the income it covers; per individual since 2023 (Revenue Service, tax caps).

dividends.summary: During the four capped years, dividends above about £300,000 of income carry no further Guernsey tax because total tax is capped at £60,000.
dividends.rate_basis: Marginal rate 0% once 20% of income exceeds £60,000.

regimes.name: Guernsey investment holding company (0% company)
regimes.description: The family funds a Guernsey company that holds the listed portfolio. Guernsey companies pay 0% income tax on investment income and there is no capital gains tax, so the company pays nothing on dividends or gains. When it pays a distribution to a Guernsey-resident member, the company must deduct 20% tax because its income was taxed at less than 20%. Profits it keeps are not taxed on the member. Foreign withholding tax on the company's dividends is a final cost.
regimes.eligibility: Any Guernsey resident can incorporate a company in Guernsey (Guernsey Registry); a Guernsey-incorporated company is tax resident in Guernsey. It must be a passive investment holder: banking, fiduciary, fund administration and other regulated activities are taxed at 10% and Guernsey property, large retail and similar at 20%; substance rules apply to some activities. US citizens are excluded (CFC/PFIC rules).
regimes.duration_note: Ordinary company rules with no time limit; the company lasts as long as the family keeps it.

capital_gains.summary: Guernsey has no capital gains tax, and companies pay income tax at a standard rate of 0% (PwC, Revenue Service), so gains realised by the holding company are not taxed.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Standard company rate 0% (PwC Guernsey corporate); no capital gains tax in Guernsey.
capital_gains.professional_trader: A company trading in securities is taxed on trading profits at the same 0% general rate; only the higher-rate activities listed by the revenue authority differ.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Foreign gains are treated the same way.

open_questions: Real estate in the island is taxed at 20% in a company; the family portfolio is listed securities, so the figure here is for those.

dividends.summary: Dividends received by a Guernsey company are income taxed at the standard 0% company rate. Foreign withholding tax suffered is not recoverable.
dividends.rate_basis: Standard company rate 0% (PwC Guernsey corporate; Revenue Service). Foreign withholding tax is lost.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 0% withholding on dividends to non-residents under domestic law; distributions to Guernsey-resident individuals carry the deduction above.
dividends.treaty_network: As the standard regime; at a 0% rate any foreign withholding on the company's dividends cannot be credited and is a final cost.
dividends.holding_company_notes: This regime models the company itself.

structure.entity: Private company limited by shares (Companies (Guernsey) Law, 2008), investment holding
structure.payout_notes: If a company's income is taxed at less than 20%, a tax charge arises when a distribution or dividend is paid to a Guernsey-resident beneficial member; the company deducts it and pays it to the Revenue Service (Revenue Service, tax information for companies). A company whose income bore 0% tax therefore deducts the full 20%. Distributions to non-residents carry no Guernsey charge. Profits kept in the company are not taxed on the member.
structure.substance_and_anti_avoidance: Loans to Guernsey-resident participators are an anti-avoidance target: preferentially priced loans are treated as income (PwC), and from 2026 repayments of non-commercial shareholder loans from personal investment companies are treated as dividends. The company files a return and a quarterly distribution report, and must show that a member is non-resident before paying without deduction. Certificate 3 covers companies with no Guernsey-resident members only.
structure.exit_and_liquidation: Liquidation distributions to a Guernsey-resident member were not researched (treatment of capital profits not confirmed). Guernsey has no exit tax on individuals.

residency.tax_residency_test: Day-count categories: principally resident (182+ days in the year); solely resident (91+ days and not 91+ days elsewhere); resident only (91-182 days, or 35+ days with 365+ days over the previous four years). Resident-only individuals may pay a standard charge (£50,000 for 2026) instead of tax on non-Guernsey income.

routes.name: Open Market housing
routes.requirements: Anyone may live in Part A Open Market property without a housing licence. Non-British/Irish nationals also need immigration permission under Bailiwick rules (UK-style; not researched in detail).

corporate.summary: General corporate rate 0%; 10% for banking, fiduciary, fund administration and similar regulated business; 20% for Guernsey property income, utilities and large retail. Pillar Two (domestic top-up tax and multinational top-up tax) from 1 January 2025 for groups with €750m+ revenue. No withholding tax on dividends to non-residents.

Excluded: price-on-application listings, and 3 Belle Vue (listed as 3 bed by Swoffers and Savills). Savills Guernsey had no 4+ bedroom lettings. A newly arriving family without a housing licence can only rent Open Market property; the two Open Market rents are GBP 4,750 and 6,000. Very thin sample: indicative only. Checked 2026-10-15 against the upper-middle-class standard.
